I was five years old, going from Kindergarten to year 1 (I would be six in February!) and that was also the year my brother got a brand spanking new Sega Mega Drive (16-bits! Wandering a fantasy land, killing monsters, helping people, solving riddles. I couldn't finish it but I learnt a lot from watching my brother play it.

I was super excited to be inheriting this amazing console and the games. I knew my brother would still claim ownership of the console, he was already practically an adult at ten years old and could do whatever he wanted! But the NES would be in my room so it would be technically mine. Good enough for me!

I actually woke up early that morning and found the sack of presents hanging off the end of my bed. It wasn't even dawn yet. I got out of bed, carefully lifted the bell mum put on top of the toy sack (cupping it underneath so the ringer wouldn't clang about), disabled her "kids are awake alarm" and pulled everything out of the sack one by one. Each time I reached in for a present I would pray it would be the specific rectangular box I was hoping for, but it wasn't.

No NES game in my stocking.

Surely this had to be some mistake? Had to be. I know! My sister and I share a room. Quite possibly, they put my game in her stocking by mistake!

So, I crept from my bed to hers in the opposite corner, lifted her bell gently, set it down without ringing, and went through all her presents. By this time the sky was beginning to lighten and I had a faint idea of what I was looking at. Lots of soft things. Lots of too-big rectangular boxes. A couple of boxes just like mine. We often got matching presents because we're so close in age. This year we got matching cassette tape decks. They were pretty cool! But as I went through all my sisters presents it began to dawn on me. Nothing in there either. No NES game for the console I was to inherit that very morning.

I was devastated. I actually went back to bed and sooked at that point, sleeping in until my sister happily woke me and declaring it Christmas!

I woke up, pretending to be excited for my younger sister. I didn't want to ruin her Christmas. She pulled out all her toys and I pretended to be surprised and excited. We did our little dance and already set up our haul in nice piles and compared. Hers was slightly larger but it was more unstable as many of her toys were soft and cuddly things.

Eventually my brother and my mother got up too. My sister and I were still in our room playing. I had some ninja turtles and was setting them against each other at my bedside, with the top of my bed being the "streets" and under the bed being the "sewer". I was enjoying myself despite my disappointment, and looking forward to the annual feast at my grandparent's place. No matter! I was getting an entire console and library of a dozen or so games, and when the adults were done being boring they would set it up for me in my room and I could play whenever I wanted and wouldn't have to hide under the bed out of sight and silent while my brother played in his own room at the back of the house!

Then my brother comes in, smiling. That was unnerving. Big brothers only smile on very rare occasions and even more rarely for pleasant reasons. He had a box in his hands. It was a Mega Drive box!

"For me?!" I ask, gob-smacked.

"Yep!" He hands it over.

I couldn't believe it! I wasn't getting an NES, I was getting a Mega Drive! And wow, the box was rattling!

"Open it!" he says.

So I do.

Inside is an NES, hastily packed up with a library of games. I try not to let me disappoint be seen.

"I want the box back." He says.

I nod, and put the box down carefully and take out the games.

Maybe, just maybe...

No, I couldn't all the games, and fondle the golden Zelda II cartridge carefully, lovingly, wishing I had its twin. I sigh. A big sigh for a small five year old.

"Did you check under the tree yet?" He asked. "That's where I got my Mega Drive."

My eyes went wide. Those sneaky parents! They didn't put all the presents in the sack at the end of my bed!

HOLY SHIT!!

MAYBE, JUST MAYBE!!

I rush out there, dragging my sister along behind me, genuinely excited for the first time since I'd awoken the second time, and she spots her giant battery operated roller-blading doll that she wanted (and which never worked but which always managed to fall over) and she goes ballistic.

And underneath it all, the smallest present under the tree, but the epitome of the phrase "good things come in small packages", was a small rectangular box.

The Mother-Fucking Legend of Zelda for NES. Gold cartridge, shining like a Christmas miracle in the pink and already too-warm Australian summer dawn.

I devoured that game for the entire five weeks of holiday left until school went back and I was sorted in to year one. By the time school went back I'd walked from one end of Hyrule to the other and saved the princess with my very own save file with my own goddamn name on it. I was a fucking hero!

And that's the story of the best game I ever got for the best Christmas ever.
